mara_1.title: The Bow at First Snow
mara_1.author: Mara, copyist
pages:
[a pressed-dark thumb stains the outer margin]

At the first stone, lower the head before the foot crosses its shadow. The road begins with yielding.
The north copy says the head bows once. The hearth copy says once for every name present. Neither names who counts.
A child asked whether kneeling was the same. It is not. Kneeling stays; the Bow passes and rises.
Snow filled the cut marks, but the oldest groove remained dark. Wear remembers what ink forgets.
Vaun carried ore when he bowed. Orin carried nothing. The stone did not distinguish them.
The reader beside me mouthed every line and never bent. I copied her posture before I understood the warning.
Do not bow to the lamp. The lamp witnesses. The marker receives the act.
Later hands added a seventh space and then scraped it level. The scrape is newer than the road.
The procession may pause between stones. It may not change their order to suit the living.
At thaw, the shadow moved. The instruction did not: begin where the first kept name fell.

mara_2.title: Offerings at the Low Hearth
mara_2.author: Mara, copyist
pages: An offering is not discarded wealth. It is the thing whose absence follows you out of the room.

[a pressed-dark thumb stains the lower margin]

Carry the chosen piece past the second mark. Do not set it down while another hand still walks empty.
Ore, seed, written name, and worked bone are all recorded. A copied token is refused without anger.
The hearth clerk weighed gifts until Vaun broke the scale. The debt survived the instrument.
Six hands may bring six unlike things. Equality of weight was never the custom.
A returned gift is entered twice: once as offered, once as taken back. The second entry is the heavier.
Do not take from a companion so that you may appear to give. The Record knows only ownership.
The poorest offerings have the longest notes. The rich entries are neat and brief.
Someone wrote LIGHT in the goods column. A later hand crossed it out and wrote WITNESS.
Nothing is burned at the low hearth. The leaving of it is enough.

mara_3.title: Six Ways to the Kept Light
mara_3.author: Mara, copyist
pages: The mason's road descends in counted landings. The pilgrim's road descends whenever courage fails.
The water road is drawn backward. Face it to the pool or mistake departure for return.
The watch road is measured in hours without sleep. No bell shortens it.

[a pressed-dark thumb stains the inner margin]

At the fourth cut, leave the written route. Follow the worn floor to the light that no closing docket quenched.
The offering road and the bow road cross. Neither cancels the other.
The warm road promises a wall. Its stones are absent when counted by hand.
A route copied without its mistakes is a new lie. Preserve the corrections.
Every edition places the last landing lower. The building, inconveniently, has only one.
The kept light is not the brightest lamp. It is the one whose extinguishing was never entered.
I have drawn all six roads. I have walked from this desk to none of them.

mara_4.title: The Marker Procession
mara_4.author: Mara, copyist
pages: The founding order flatters the founders. The fall order tells the truth.
First the bearer, then the reader, then the drowned, the mason, the sleepless, and the liar.
A procession is not six visits. The bodies between the stones are part of the sentence.

[a pressed-dark thumb stains the outer margin]

Keep the fourth turn narrow. Pass the mason's cut shoulder to shoulder; after it, no one walks ahead.
Children raced the route and were made to begin again, laughing. The clerk did not record the laughter.
A missing walker leaves no empty footprint. Count voices at the turn instead.
The liar's stone is last in fall order, though his account puts him near the first hearth.
Do not reverse the line on the return. Return is not part of the rite.
One old diagram shows a seventh rail outside the procession. It bears no keeper's mark.
I can recite the order faster than anyone. This has never made me present in it.

mara_5.title: What Is Owed Below
mara_5.author: Mara, copyist
pages: At the last landing, names are spoken by others. No one witnesses their own name alone.
The lamp is capped before the gifts are laid. Light arriving early changes the meaning.
The floor accepts a crowd but the old drawing shows six places. The drawing is not a limit.
A witness may refuse the Record and remain a witness. Acceptance is not obedience.
The prior company brought answers in perfect order. Their witness column remained blank.

[a pressed-dark thumb stains the lower margin]

At the sixth and final count, descend together. Bow at the unbroken light; leave no living name at the door.
What each person brings must be theirs to miss. Words copied from this page are not a gift.
When all have risen, look for the place the six rails fail to enclose.
The Record calls completion an accepting. The older hand calls it being seen and surviving.
I know this ending by heart. I have never stood beneath it.

sella_1.title: Near Shore
sella_1.author: Sella
pages: Teacher says begin at the bank, not the water. The bank does not stay where I draw it.

( . )
      (     )

one stone; two rings before the reeds move
Mara lent me the black pencil. It makes my fingers look older.
The little bird drinks without making a face in the water. I tried and got my nose wet.
There are six dry markers from the school door. I counted twice because Brann said once is wishing.
Mother tied a pale thread to my sleeve. It came loose before supper.
The near shore gives my letters back with their wrong hands.
I drew the bow marker too tall. Orin said the stone would enjoy the compliment.
Rain makes more circles than stones do. They interrupt one another and nobody wins.
Vaun says never pocket a pretty thing from an offering place. I put the blue chip back.
The bird flew past the last post and came home. This seems important.
Teacher wrote: SELLA, KEEP TO THE NEAR SHORE. I copied it exactly.

sella_2.title: Rain Count
sella_2.author: Sella
pages: Small rain makes the pool look furry. Heavy rain erases the pool entirely.
The gutter drips seven times after the bell, unless the wind is rude.

(( . ))
    (       )

three rings reach the chalk line
Iss says counting is safer indoors. He says many safe things.
A drowned worm lay on the step. I moved it into soil though it was probably too late.
The third marker holds water in its top cut. A sparrow bathes there.
My reflected seven looks like the mark Mara uses when a line is missing.
Orin told me not to scratch numbers into civic stone. I used chalk after that.
The rain stopped while I sharpened the pencil. This is poor cooperation.
Six coats hung at school. Mine made seven. The peg was already there.
At dusk the far water turns the same grey as the path. That is how feet make mistakes.
I promised to come straight home. I meant it when I wrote it.

sella_3.title: Bird Lessons
sella_3.author: Sella
pages: Deep-birds are not canaries, even if everyone calls them that when frightened.
A bird's eye is on the side so it can watch leaving and returning at once.
The yellow one prefers seed cracked under a spoon. It throws the rest at us.
I drew both wings equal. The bird declined to demonstrate this courtesy.

((( . )))
  (         )

five rings; the bird stepped through the last
Teacher says feathers hold air between their little branches. Warmth is mostly trapped nothing.
The coop goes silent before the watch bell. Brann believes this is a kind of warning.
I named one bird Farther because it always chose the far perch.
Vaun fixed the latch with offering wire and then complained that the birds owed him.
Mara can copy a wing perfectly but hers never looks ready to move.
A loose feather on water points wherever the surface tells it.
If I had wings I would still use the road. Roads have people on them.

sella_4.title: Reed Water
sella_4.author: Sella
pages: Reeds make a wall that moves aside. This is more honest than a stone wall.
The green stems cut my thumb. Water found the cut before I did.
There is a path where the reeds lean outward, but only from the hill can I see it.
I heard a bell under the wind. Brann says sound cannot be underneath another sound.
The mud kept one shoe and gave it back after I asked badly.
Seven stems grew through the old basket. Six were tied together.

(((( . ))))
(             )

seven rings touch the bent reed
The surface writes faster than I do and rubs everything out at once.
Iss knew which path I meant before I finished telling him. He smiled.
At noon the far bank looks near. At evening the near bank forgets its edge.
I left a white stone where the reeds fold back. It was gone the next day.
Teacher wrote DO NOT GO PAST THE REEDS. I practiced the letters twice.

sella_5.title: The Far Edge
sella_5.author: Sella
pages: The far water has no school bell in it. I checked by waiting.
My footsteps filled before I turned around. The lake dislikes evidence.
A black bird followed the shore without flapping. It may have been only very far away.
There should be six markers. I found the place after six and it felt like another.
The old shrine has no warm lamp. Someone cleaned the soot away and left the cold.
I could see home in the water but not when I looked up.
The pale thread on my sleeve caught on a thorn. I did not go back for it.
A sign faced the lake. Its dry side was blank.
I counted first to last, then last to first. The middle would not stay the same.
The reeds bent where there was no wind. I thought something small had passed.

(((((( . ))))))

eleven rings reach the stone that is not in the row
If this book comes home before I do, tell them I followed the margin and not the girl.
